first.rationale: Three pressures compete for the single experiment slot. Promotional pricing is tempting given the competitor's aggressive entry pricing, but memory_73 carries an explicit caveat (pooled cohorts after mid-test redefinition) and a price-matching response risks eroding sustainable revenue quality and inviting a margin race — exactly the failure mode the objective warns against. I want to verify memory_73's original record before ever acting on it, even though I'm not choosing it this week. Onboarding completion and activation are both down this quarter, and memory_31 and memory_86 (unflagged, durable) both support that simplifying signup/onboarding reliably lifts SMB activation and completion — this is the more defensible lever for sustainable qualified revenue since it fixes a real degrading funnel rather than reacting to a competitor's short-term pricing move. I'm also verifying memory_31 directly since it's the oldest and most load-bearing claim for this action, to confirm the original effect size and scope before committing capacity. Given onboarding changes can affect lead/customer quality (fewer fields may reduce qualification signal), I'm flagging downstream value risk and keeping the test small and guarded rather than a broad rollout, preserving room to reassess promotional pricing next cycle once memory_73 is re-verified.
